skill.recurring_jobs.body.title: SKILL.md
skill.recurring_jobs.body.content:
# Recurring jobs

Start a new Soulstream agent session at a scheduled time or on node connection. Examples include checking status each morning, creating a report tomorrow, and checking a home PC when it connects.

For an assignee following up on their own card, use `set_card_status` with `status: awaiting_verification`, the wake time in `wake_at`, and what the session is waiting for in `waiting_for`. Follow the status procedure in card-work.

```link
call: card-work
when: When a card assignee waits for verification of their own card
```

## Create a job

1. Define the work and trigger. Use `list_nodes` or other tools to confirm the execution node and agent, and pick an accessible folder. The execution node must be connected at creation. The server checks the agent and model on that node and access to the folder. The trigger node can differ from the execution node.
2. Give `create_recurring_job` the common fields `name`, `prompt`, `idempotency_key`, `timezone`, and the execution `node_id`, `agent_id`, `model_preset`, and `folder_id`. Use a preset ID or `null` for the agent's default. Set `timezone` to a valid name such as `Asia/Seoul`. Jobs start enabled unless you set `enabled: false`.
3. Supply exactly one trigger below. Reuse the same `idempotency_key` when retrying the same creation request. Use a new key for a new job. Keep the returned job ID and version, then verify settings with `get_recurring_job`.

### Repeat on a schedule

Supply `schedule_expressions` as an array of five-field cron strings, in minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week order. For example, `timezone: "Asia/Seoul"` and `schedule_expressions: ["0 9 * * 1-5"]` runs at 9 a.m. on weekdays in Seoul. Any matching expression triggers a run. Matches at the same time count once. Before creating the job, pass the same time zone and array to `preview_recurring_schedule` to see the next five runs.

### Run once at a set time

Supply a future ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset in `run_at`, such as `2027-01-15T09:00:00+09:00`. You can use `Z` for UTC. The `timezone` field is also required.

### Run when a node connects

Set `event_trigger` to `type: "node_connected"` with the Soulstream tool. The web supports creating repeating and one-time jobs. The app supports repeating jobs. Node-triggered jobs require the tool.

- `node_id` is the node to watch. It defaults to the execution `node_id` and can differ from it.
- `settle_seconds` is how long the node must stay connected. It defaults to 180 and accepts integers from 0 to 3600.
- `cooldown_seconds` is the wait before triggering again. It defaults to 3600 and accepts integers from 0 to 604800.
- `repeat` defaults to `false`. Set it to `true` to run on each later connection that meets the conditions.

To observe a home PC connecting from an always-on server, use the server for the execution `node_id` and the home PC for `event_trigger.node_id`. To run on the home PC itself, use it as the execution node too and make sure it is connected at creation.

```json
{
  "name": "Check home PC connection",
  "prompt": "When the home PC connects, check the target node and record the result in this folder. Finish after checking or recording why the node is inaccessible.",
  "idempotency_key": "home-pc-connection-check-unique-key",
  "timezone": "Asia/Seoul",
  "node_id": "execution-server-node-id",
  "agent_id": "execution-agent-id",
  "model_preset": null,
  "folder_id": "results-folder-id",
  "event_trigger": {
    "type": "node_connected",
    "node_id": "home-pc-node-id",
    "settle_seconds": 180,
    "cooldown_seconds": 3600,
    "repeat": false
  }
}
```

Replace the sample IDs and prompt with the actual targets and completion criteria. The new session has no current conversation context. In `prompt`, provide the task, target, background, output location, and when to finish.

## What happens during execution

- The watched node must stay connected for `settle_seconds`. If the job is created while the node is connected, the timer starts from the existing connection. If it already elapsed, the job may run at the next check.
- A reconnection within 600 seconds counts as the same connection, including after an orchestrator restart. If already run for that connection, the job waits for a new one. With `repeat: true`, a new connection must also satisfy cooldown.
- If the execution node is offline, the run enters `waiting_for_node`. Connection-triggered and manual runs wait until the node connects. Recurring and one-time scheduled runs require the node to reconnect within `late_run_window_seconds`, a positive integer that defaults to 1800. After that the run becomes `skipped_late`. If several recurring times were missed, run only the latest within the window.
- A job with a pending or active run does not start another overlapping session. Scheduled and manual runs record a skip. A connection trigger is checked again when the active run ends.
- A one-time `run_at` job or a node-triggered job with `repeat: false` deletes the job and run history once session creation is confirmed. Tell the new session where to keep any results needed later.

## Inspect and change jobs

- Use `list_recurring_jobs` for the list and `get_recurring_job(job_id)` for settings and version. Use `include_archived: true` for archived jobs.
- Pass `job_id`, the latest `expected_version`, and changed fields to `update_recurring_job`. If there is a conflict, reread and use the latest values. Set `enabled: false` to pause and `enabled: true` to resume. Supply a future `run_at` when resuming a one-time job whose scheduled time passed.
- Resend the full `event_trigger` when changing its conditions. To switch between recurring, one-time, and node triggers, archive the old job and create a new one.
- Run once now with `run_recurring_job(job_id, idempotency_key)`, even when paused. Reuse the key when retrying the same manual run.
- Archive with `archive_recurring_job(job_id, expected_version)`. Active sessions keep running.
- Use `list_recurring_job_runs(job_id)` for remaining run states and `session_id`. Check `waiting_for_node`, `skipped_late`, `skipped_overlap`, and error reasons. For a one-time job or `repeat: false` trigger, history is deleted once session creation is confirmed.

# Soulstream features and settings (soulstream-guide)

Use the guide installed on this server to answer questions about Soulstream features, settings, persistent sessions, coding agent sign-in, opening atom, installation, updates, removal, or configuration files.

## Read the guide

The atom guide folder is separate from this skill and is read directly.

1. For the full guide, call `mcp__atom__compile_subtree(node_id="{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide}}", depth=null)`. It contains eight cards.
2. For one topic, use `compile_subtree` with its node ID below.

## Guide cards

- What's installed and how to open it, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.install}}`. Installer arguments, components, SSH tunnels and ports, and Tailscale.
- First window and persistent sessions, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.first_window}}`. Startup screen, how to turn it off, the default persistent session, and three screens shown when there is no persistent session.
- Settings, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.settings}}`. Four groups, tab roles, and admin-only tabs.
- Coding agent sign-in, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.coding_login}}`. Connect or reconnect Claude, Codex, and Antigravity. Diagnose failures or use SSH.
- Open atom, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.atom_open}}`. When the "Open atom" button appears and what to do if it is missing.
- Reinstall and update, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.update}}`. Update steps, what changes, what persists, recovery, one-time seeding of instructions, and removal.
- Configuration files and key environment variables, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.config_files}}`. File locations and relevant keys.
- Settings reset on reinstall, `{{node_id:common.soulstream_guide.env_owned}}`. Environment variables and managed files owned by the installer.

## Answer

1. Read the card for the question and use only its facts. If it does not name a menu, button, or value, say what is unknown and where to check.
2. Give short navigation steps. For example, open "Settings" → "Coding agent logins", choose a node, and click "Connect" on the Codex row.
3. If the installed guide and current screen differ, follow the screen. New guide revisions do not automatically appear on existing servers.
4. If an admin-only tab such as "Coding agent logins" is missing, ask whether the user is signed in as an administrator.

## User actions

- Have users sign in through the dashboard sign-in sheet or an SSH session they open. Keep login codes, authentication URLs, tokens, and passwords out of the conversation, even if the user already pasted them.
- Leave CLI sign-in to the user. Keep admin password files and configuration files containing secret values out of the response.
- Give installation, update, and removal commands or navigation paths for the user to run on their server.

## Persistent sessions (PAS)

Persistent session agents can read and use `load_skill`, `search_skills`, and `compile_subtree`. They lack file editing, Bash, and atom write tools. Explain where to change settings.

- For a settings tab, go to "Settings" and select "Coding agent logins", "Agent profiles", "Default session model", or the tab for the setting.
- For a server file, connect over SSH and edit it directly.
- For the guide itself, click "Open atom" and edit the guide under Agents → Common → Soulstream Guide.

skill.daily_review.body.content:
# daily-review

Review recent work once a day to keep the workspace organized and its knowledge current. The "Daily review" recurring job calls this skill. Use Soulstream MCP (`list_cards`, `list_sessions`, `get_session_turn_summaries`, `list_folders`) and atom tools only. Leave external collection scripts out. The job starts a new session. If this session has no card, create and assign yourself a "Daily review" card first. As assignee of this recurring job card, mark it `done` when finished.

```link
call: card-work
when: When creating or completing the "Daily review" card
note: Follow the sections on creating cards and assignee completion of recurring job cards
```

## 0. Stop early when little work has closed

1. Use `list_cards` to review `done` cards, newest first. Exclude "Daily review" cards. Count cards closed after the last run according to `list_recurring_job_runs` or card notes. If the last run is unknown, count the past day.
2. If fewer than three cards closed, skip changes and questions. Record "Skipped because only N cards closed" on a check item and finish with `set_card_status(status: done)`.

## 1. Gather evidence

- Read the requests and closure notes of newly closed cards with `get_card`. When there are several, start with titles and status boards and read details only where needed.
- Use `get_session_turn_summaries` for the same period instead of full transcripts.
- Use `list_folders` to inspect folder organization.

## 2. Check three areas

### 2-1. Organize folders

- Consider a new folder if "Workspace" has eight or more cards excluding "Daily review", and at least three share a subject or repository.
- After approval, create it with `create_folder`. In `initial_context`, add one line of `guidance` with the topic and project card location. Add `atomReferences` for the Project > <name> node so later sessions receive the project in `<page_context>`. Set all five fields: `{instance: "atom", nodeId, nodeTitle, depth: 2, titlesOnly: true}`. Move related cards with `move_card`.
- To link project knowledge to an existing folder, add an `atom_ref` block with `batch_page_operations`.

### 2-2. Review instructions and skills

- Suggest a change only after a procedure repeated at least twice or the user set a standing expectation such as "always" or "from now on". Skip one-off events and guesses.
- Start at the narrowest scope. Put project-specific precautions under Development Notes in the Project > <name> card. Use `skill-creator` for workflows repeated across projects. Reserve global rules for standards that apply to all work.
- Use `mistake-record` when you know the cause of a mistake or incident and need to prevent it from recurring.

### 2-3. Find gaps in project knowledge

- Suggest a project card if a closed card covered a repository missing under Project in atom. If a card exists but is stale and the structure or decisions changed, suggest updating it.
- Suggest `atom-tree-cleanup` when the Project > <name> tree has more than 20 decision cards.

## 3. Ask and finish

- Collect candidates into one `ask_card_question`, at most once per day. Give one line per candidate explaining what and why. Offer "Do all", "Do some", and "Skip today".
- Do the approved work on this card. Create folders and organize project cards directly. Use `skill-creator` and `general-create-rule` for new skills or rules. Ask again about a rejected candidate only if the evidence changes.
- With no candidates, add a one-line check item result and mark the card `done` without a question.

## Boundaries

Leave other cards open and in place unless the user authorizes a closure or deletion. Keep active cards in their current folders. Use MCP tools without editing files or running shell commands.

# skill-creator

Create or revise a skill card in atom under Agents > Common > skills. Keep the skill there without workspace copies such as `.claude/skills`.

## When to create one

Use a skill when the same procedure has repeated at least twice or the user says "always" or "from now on". Leave out one-off work. Put project-specific procedures in the project card's notes. Promote only standards that apply to all work into rules.

## Five steps

1. **Search for related skills.** Use `search_skills` and `find-skill` to find duplicates and related skills. Revise an existing body when it already covers the procedure.
2. **Write the entry.** Under `skills`, create a structure card named for the skill. Write YAML with `description` (one or two sentences on when to use it), `body_node_id` (the node_id of the SKILL.md card), and when needed, `uses` (related skill names) and `probe_intents` (example requests that should trigger it).
3. **Write the body.** Under the structure card, add a `SKILL.md` card. Use `call`, `include`, and `pick` blocks to refer to other skills under `skill-link-blocks`. Within 4,000 characters, write the purpose, steps, boundaries, and completion report in that order.
4. **Add scripts if needed.** Use `$AGENT_COMMON_FILES_DIR/skills/<skill name>/`. Prefer standalone Node `.mjs` files without external packages. Use `.local/tmp` for temporary outputs. Give custom skills a separate name to preserve bundled files such as `html-make`.
5. **Link and verify.** Add a symlink under the target agent's `skills`. Call `load_skill(name=<skill name>)` once and confirm it expands the body without errors in `links` or `warnings`. If it fails to trigger, revise `description`.

## Report

Include the skill name, card location, linked agent, and `load_skill` result.

skill.git_setup.body.content:
# git-setup

Set up Git and repository access for a worker on this server before code changes, pull requests, or worktree operations. Keep passwords and personal access tokens (PATs) out of chats and card questions.

## 1. Use Settings first

If the user can set up Git, direct them to "Settings" → "Agents and nodes" → "Git and repositories" (Admin). They can set each node's Git name and email, generate an SSH public key, and clone a repository there. Follow the next steps only when the agent needs to set it up.

## 2. Set up from the worker shell

Use non-interactive commands in the agent shell. Commands that wait for input stall the session.

1. **Identity.** Check `git config --global user.name` and `user.email` for the account running the worker. Ask the user for any missing values and set them.
2. **Authentication.** Use HTTPS for read-only public clones. For a private repository or push access, reuse an existing `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` or generate it as the worker with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -C <name>`. Show only `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` in `ask_card_question`. Have the user add it to their host, such as GitHub or GitLab, as an SSH key or deploy key. Continue after the `했어` (shown as "I did it") answer. Keep the private key out of all output.
3. **Clone.** Use `.projects/<repository>` under the worker's `WORKTREE_PROJECTS_ROOT`. To avoid an interactive host key prompt on the first SSH clone, use `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new" git clone <address> <path>` or run `ssh-keyscan <host> >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts` before cloning. This is the base checkout. Confirm the repository appears in `list_worktrees`.
4. **Pull request automation.** Set it up only when needed. Have the user run sign-in in their host terminal so interactive `gh auth login --web` does not stall the agent. On Linux, provide `sudo -u soulstream gh auth login`. On Windows, provide `gh auth login`. Once the user says it is done, verify with `gh auth status`.
5. **Record.** In atom under Project > <repository name>, add the repository path, default branch, build commands, and checks to Overview and Paths. Create the card if needed.

## Report

List identity setup, authentication method, clone path, `list_worktrees` result, remaining user actions, and any checks you could not complete.

skill.html_make.body.content:
# html-make

Create one HTML report, dashboard, introduction, or summary with one of three presets: Index, Apple, or Astryx.

## 1. Choose one preset

1. Use Index, Apple, or Astryx as specified by the user.
2. Default to Index for a new document.
3. For an existing document without a redesign request, keep the root `data-design`.
4. If two presets are requested or the choice is genuinely unclear, ask the user to choose one.

## 2. Read the selected preset shard

Use `mcp__atom__compile_subtree` with the shard node_id from the table for the selected preset. Read only that shard.

```link
include: html-design-preset
```

Follow its token table, layout, components, and restrictions. If you need a missing value, add it to the root token block under a role-based name.

Check how to implement browser features such as dialogs, forms, scrolling, transitions, and animations before writing them.

```link
call: modern-web-guidance
when: When adding browser features such as dialogs, forms, scrolling, or motion
```

## 3. Build the document

1. Use `$SCRATCH_WORKSPACE_DIR/.local/tmp/<name>/` for temporary work and `.local/artifacts/` for the deliverable.
2. Write `tokens.css` with only the root token block and `style.css` with rules whose token values use `var()`. Combine the files into one `<style>` for the final HTML.
3. For English, use `<html lang="en" data-design="index|apple|astryx">`. Set `lang` to match the document language.
4. Use tables, diagrams (SVG or HTML and CSS), and visual hierarchy where they communicate more clearly than paragraphs. Omit redundant explanations of visible elements.
5. Use a system font fallback stack and keep the single file self-contained without external CDNs or images.
6. Use at least 16px for body text and 13px for all text. For Korean text, use `word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: break-word` to preserve words while allowing long strings to wrap. Support light and dark modes, visible keyboard focus, and reduced motion.
7. Keep rows of numeric tiles away from the area immediately below document and section titles.
8. Use `user-select` only in one `<style data-ui="selection">` block. Keep body text, tables, and code selectable.

## 4. Check CSS

The bundled checker looks for colors, sizes, fonts, radii, and spacing set directly outside the token file in the working directory's `.css` files. Create an empty baseline once.

```bash
echo '{}' > <work-dir>/ui-css-baseline.json
node "$AGENT_COMMON_FILES_DIR/skills/html-make/scripts/check-ui-css.mjs" --root <work-dir> --config "$AGENT_COMMON_FILES_DIR/skills/html-make/scripts/ui-css-check.config.json"
```

- Exit 0 passes. For exit 1, use each reported `file:line: original text` to move the value into `tokens.css` and reference it with `var()`. Run the check again.
- After a pass, combine `tokens.css` and `style.css` into the single HTML file.
- If the checker is missing or cannot run, report it and inspect the styles directly.

## 5. Deliver the result

1. Save the completed HTML file in `.local/artifacts/`.
2. Check whether file storage is connected. If it is, use `register_attachment` to attach the file to a document or card for the dashboard viewer. Share the attachment link.
3. If `register_attachment` reports that storage is not configured, share the workspace path and record a Markdown summary with `create_markdown_document`. For attachments, tell the user to connect storage in "Settings" → "Records and administration" → "File storage".
4. If you can inspect the UI, check light mode, dark mode, and phone width once each. Report views you could not inspect.

```link
call: ui-design
when: When creating or changing a Soulstream product screen
note: The three presets are for published documents. Use ui-design for product screens
```

## Boundaries

- Use a single preset. For a new document with no specified style, use Index.
- Keep shadows, rounded corners, expand icons, and side navigation out of Index documents.
- Render diagrams instead of leaving ASCII art or Mermaid source.
- Keep bundled files under `$AGENT_COMMON_FILES_DIR/skills/html-make/` intact. Use a separately named skill to customize them.

## Report

1. Preset and whether it was requested or the default
2. Save path and attachment status
3. CSS check result
4. Views checked in light, dark, and phone layouts, and any unverified scope
